title: a reseal on a host that cannot run a tooth does not replace a seal from a host that can
intention: reseal() does not persist a record over a standing green seal for the same source fingerprint when every tooth the new run failed reads UNRAN; it leaves that seal byte-identical and says so loudly, and a run where a tooth actually FAILs still writes red.
why: Measured: 2026-11-20 on akiendell (Windows): cc_0's Linux landing of 80a2-fix (a2f477928) resealed bin/proofs/test_cairn_runs_from_cmd_with_no_bash.py on Linux, where teeth 1 and 3 read UNRAN (cairn.cmd is Windows-only), and persist_validation REPLACED my green 3 of 3 Windows seal with that red. The replacement voided 380d524e6e9c's hollow evidence and left the proof red on main until I resealed on Windows (bdce17bf1) and re-ran the hollow (1e958634f). Outline 9.4.8.1 already reads a not-run tooth as not-run, never red; the seal write has no such reading.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured); Law 5 (the repo is the state of the machine: a crossing's record is committed where it lands); Law 9 (green is earned).
how: A hypothesis, not a settled shape: in reseal(), before the write, read the standing seal for the same source_fingerprint; when it is green and every failing tooth of the new run reads UNRAN, return an outcome that names the kept seal and writes nothing. A failure that is not UNRAN, a standing seal on other bytes, or no standing seal writes exactly as today. 50ac45cde4dd fixes the verdict's reading of such a seal; this fixes the write that destroys the evidence the verdict reads.

clauses.claim: a fixture proof with a green Windows seal, resealed on Linux with every failing tooth UNRAN, keeps the seal file byte-identical and the result says the seal was kept and why
a reseal where a tooth actually FAILs still writes red over the green seal
a reseal over a standing seal on other bytes (fingerprint differs) writes as before

D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause.
